newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 25.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 25.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN Golfer Greg Norman beat fellow Queenslander Wayne Grady by eight shots yesterday to win his fifth Australian Open golf championship in front of a 30,000-strong crowd. Page 1.

Cricketer Steve Waugh's groin injury, sustained after a match against the West Indies yesterday at the Gabba, is being assessed this morning, with doubts about his participation in the second test in Sydney on Friday. Page 19. --
Former Ireland fly-half Tony Ward has expressed his disappointment in the latest Wallabies team, joining others in claiming the team has lost the attacking flair of the past. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD
After John Eales fractured his right eye socket on Saturday, ruling him out of the rest of the Wallaby tour, Tim Horan is poised to take over as the new Australian captain. Page 26.

Cricketer Craig McDermott made a surprise appearance at the Australian team warmup before the third day of the first Test against the West Indies, indicating the bowler is on the road to recovery. Page 27.
An injury to stand-in Bushrangers skipper Tony Dodemaide during a match against England A At Princes Park has placed controversial Victorian veteran Dean Jones back in charge. Page 27.
THE AGE
Punters who bet early on Saintly for yesterday's Japan Cup were badly burnt by the surprise scratching of the horse, collectively losing more than A$100,000. Page 2.
Australian golfer Karrie Webb tied with American Emilee Klein for the lead in the US LPGA Tour Championship yesterday, putting her in the running for the US prizemoney title. Page 7.

Australian Olympic sprinter Dean Capobianco yesterday said he was furious with the way the International Amateur Athletic Federation handled his case concerning the use of steroids in competition. Capobianco has been banned from competition. Page 9.
HERALD SUN

An impressive 6.688 second pass down the 400m track at the Calder Park raceway has been recorded by four-time Australian Funny Car champion Peter Russo at the Night of the Nitro Drag Racing race meeting on Saturday. Page 76.
The Australian inquiry that cleared Olympic sprinter Dean Capobianco of drug charges was criticised by the International Amateur Athletic federation yesterday. Page 77.
A controversial soccer ruling that led to a tie between the Lakers and the Melbourne Knights has angered the Melbourne team who have called it a "disgraceful decision". Page 82.
DAILY TELEGRAPH

Bart Cummings repeated his threat of never bringing another horse to Japan yesterday unless an uninterrupted passage can be arranged, and pleaded for a direct flight to bring his sick horse Saintly home after scratching it from the Japan Cup. Page 29.
The Sydney Blues have been knocked out 4-0 in their baseball series against the Adelaide Giants, leaving commentators to wonder if they can even by a playoff contender this season. Page 31.
Australian Cara Honeychurch has won the women's world tenpin bowling championship after a week of competition in Dundonald, Northern Ireland. Page 32.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
